content.text:
Yes. The specs in `e2e/test/scenarios/embedding/` use the same runner, the same `restore()` snapshots, and the same `H.*` helpers as other e2e specs. But they have six special characteristics.

## 1. The test visits a page that the test itself makes, not the Metabase app

A normal spec opens a Metabase route. An embedding spec opens an embed URL or a fake host page, and then looks inside an iframe.

```text
normal spec                       embedding spec (embed.js)
  cy.visit("/question/1")           cy.intercept("GET", "/sdk-iframe-test-page", { body: <generated HTML> })
  cy.findByText(...)                cy.visit("/sdk-iframe-test-page")
                                      <script src="embed.js">
                                      window.metabaseConfig = {...}
                                      <metabase-dashboard dashboard-id=1>
                                    getSimpleEmbedIframeContent()   ← waits 40 s for iframe[data-iframe-loaded]
                                      .findByText(...)
```

The Metabase host page is used as the origin, so the specs do not need `cy.origin` or cross-origin settings (0 specs use them).

## 2. Most specs sign out after setup

```text
setup (as admin)                     test (as anonymous visitor)
  restore()                            visitEmbeddedPage(payload)
  cy.signInAsAdmin()                     cy.exec("node e2e-jwt-sign.js ...")   ← signs the JWT in Node
  activateToken("pro-self-hosted")       cy.signOut()                          ← always
  PUT /api/setting/enable-embedding-*    cy.visit("/embed/dashboard/<jwt>#...")
  publish card / dashboard
```

The SDK specs log in with JWT. `mockAuthProviderAndJwtSignIn` intercepts the fake auth provider URL and returns a signed user JWT. Guest embed specs set `embedding-secret-key` to a known secret.

## 3. Setup is mostly in one helper

The 16 specs in `sdk-iframe-embedding/` do not call `restore()` directly. They call `prepareSdkIframeEmbedTest()`, which does all of the setup:

```text
prepareSdkIframeEmbedTest({ withToken, enabledAuthMethods, signOut })
  restore()
  cy.signInAsAdmin()
  activateToken("bleeding-edge")           ← default
  PUT enable-embedding-simple
  intercept card / dashcard / dashboard queries
  setupMockAuthProviders  (jwt | saml | api-key)
  mockEmbedJsToDevServer()                 ← local only, see below
```

## 4. They depend on settings and tokens more than other specs

| Pattern | embedding (46 specs) | all other specs (367) |
|---|---|---|
| sets `enable-embedding-*` | 15 | 3 |
| sets `embedding-secret-key` | 6 | 0 |
| uses JWT | 19 | 5 |
| `window.metabaseConfig` | 13 | 0 |
| `@EE` tag | 6 | 3 |
| `@OSS` tag | 9 | 19 |

Some areas have two copies of a spec, one for each edition. For example, `common-ee` and `common-oss-and-starter` are copies, and `guest-embed-ee` and `guest-embed-oss` are copies. They test the same flow on different plans (`starter`, `pro-self-hosted`, `pro-cloud`, or no token).

## 5. Local runs and CI runs load embed.js differently

```text
mockEmbedJsToDevServer()
  if CI → do nothing (use the built embed.js)
  else  → curl localhost:8080/app/embed.js
          if found → redirect embed.js to the rspack dev server (hot reload)
```

Thus, a local run can test embed.js code that is different from the code in CI.

## 6. The static-embed specs use shared fixture data

```text
embedding/
├── embedding-questions.cy.spec.js  ──imports──▶ shared/embedding-questions.js
├── embedding-dashboard.cy.spec.js  ──imports──▶ shared/embedding-dashboard.js
└── ...                                          (question/dashboard definitions, not tests)
```

## Same as other specs

- They run with the normal `test-cypress` command and use the same CI shards. They are not in a separate CI job.
- They use the same snapshots and `H.*` helpers, and the same `@external` tag (3 specs).

result: The standard embedding e2e specs use the same runner, snapshots, and CI as other e2e specs. The differences: they visit test-generated host pages or JWT `/embed` URLs and look inside iframes (40 s waits), they sign out after admin setup, they put setup in `prepareSdkIframeEmbedTest`, they depend a lot on embedding settings, tokens, and EE/OSS spec pairs, and locally they can load embed.js from the dev server.
